saints.name: Sts. John de Brébeuf and Isaac Jogues, and Companions
saints.title: Priests and Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: The North American Martyrs, French Jesuits who carried the Gospel to the Huron and Iroquois and died for it…
biography: Eight French Jesuits, six priests and two lay helpers, of the mission of Sainte-Marie among the Hurons in New France died by torture between 1642 and 1649 amid the war of the Mohawk against the Huron. René Goupil, a surgeon and donné, was the first, tomahawked at Ossernenon in 1642.

Isaac Jogues, captured with Goupil and ritually mutilated, was ransomed by Dutch traders and returned to France, where the pope dispensed his maimed hands for the offering of Mass; sailing back to his mission, he was killed with the layman Jean de la Lande at Ossernenon in October 1646. Antoine Daniel fell in 1648 in the attack on his Huron mission of Teanaostaye.

In 1649 the Iroquois broke the Huron nation and its mission: John de Brébeuf, the apostle of the Hurons, was tortured to death with Gabriel Lalemant at St. Ignace in March, and Charles Garnier and Noël Chabanel were killed in December. Beatified in 1925 and canonized by Pius XI in 1930, the eight are the patrons of Canada, honored at the shrines of Midland and Auriesville.
saints.knownFor: Martyrdom while evangelizing the peoples of North America.

sources.text: R. G. Thwaites (ed.), The Jesuit Relations and Allied Documents (1896–1901; public domain)
